documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, physician record
Arrival 05/13/2025 14:50 by ambulance from a job site.

HPI: 29 y/o male construction worker. Per EMS and coworkers, his left arm contacted an overhead power line while he was moving equipment. No fall from height reported. Awake, alert and oriented on arrival. Severe pain in the left arm, which is swollen and red. Hx depression, hyperuricemia, kidney injury last fall attributed to allopurinol.
Home meds (per patient/old list): sertraline 50 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA. Former smoker, social alcohol.

Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 110, RR 18, T 37.2 C.
Exam: Alert, GCS 15, in distress from pain. Left forearm tense and tender throughout, swollen and erythematous; passively extending the fingers produces severe pain. Radial pulse palpable. Right arm, chest and legs without injury. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, no arrhythmia.

Labs: creatinine 1.8 (no baseline available to us), K 5.5, Ca 7.9, phos 6.2, CK 20,000. Urine dip 3+ blood, microscopy without RBCs.

Assessment: High-voltage electrical injury with compartment syndrome of the left forearm and hand. Rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuria and acute kidney injury, mild hyperkalemia.
Plan: Aggressive IV fluids targeting urine output. Cardiac monitoring. Hyperkalemia treated per protocol. Tdap updated. Hand surgery at bedside, to OR emergently for fasciotomy. Admit to surgery.

Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Operative Report: Fasciotomy
documents.author: hand surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, operative report
Date of surgery: 05/13/2025
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: Compartment syndrome, left forearm and hand, after high-voltage electrical injury.
Procedure: Fasciotomy of the left forearm, volar and dorsal; decompression of the hand compartments.
Anesthesia: General.
Findings: Tense volar and dorsal forearm compartments. Muscle swollen, pink and contractile after release. Hand compartments tight, released. No muscle debridement needed.
EBL minimal. Wounds left open with negative pressure dressing. Condition to PACU stable.
Plan: Return for wound closure in 3-5 days.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hand surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, discharge summary
Admitted 05/13/2025, discharged 05/20/2025.

Diagnoses: High-voltage electrical injury. Compartment syndrome left forearm and hand, s/p fasciotomy. Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury, resolved.

Course: Taken to the OR the evening of arrival for fasciotomy (see op note). IV fluids with close urine output monitoring; potassium normal by the next morning and creatinine back to normal within days. CK fell steadily. Returned to the OR 05/17 for delayed primary closure of the fasciotomy wounds, closed without graft. Started hand therapy in the hospital. Telemetry without arrhythmia.

Discharge labs 05/20: creatinine 1.0, CK 1,850.
Discharge exam: wounds clean and closed, sutures in. Fingers warm, sensation intact, motion limited by stiffness.

Discharge medications: acetaminophen-oxycodone 325/5 mg every 6 hours as needed, short supply. Home: sertraline 50 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: hand surgery clinic in 3 weeks, suture removal at 2 weeks, outpatient occupational therapy twice weekly. Off work until cleared by hand surgery. PCP within 1-2 weeks; recheck BMP and CK.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge summary arrived. Home since yesterday, staying with his parents for the week. Pain 5/10, taking the oxycodone pill about twice a day, plus nothing else. Dressing dry. Urine normal color now. Sertraline taking. Reviewed d/c med list with him: he is NOT on allopurinol, the hospital carried it from an old list. Appt 5/27 with PCP confirmed. Knows to go to ED for numbness, cold fingers, fever or wound drainage.

conditions.label: Traumatic compartment syndrome of left upper extremity, initial encounter

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two weeks out from the power line injury. Discharge summary, op note and ED record reviewed. Sutures came out at hand surgery on Friday. Pain 3/10, down to one oxycodone at night and stopping. Hand stiff, starts OT twice a week next week. Sleeping poorly the first few nights, replaying it; better now. Mood a bit down being off work, PHQ-9 6. No SI. Workers' comp case opened by his employer.

Meds: sertraline 50 daily. Not on allopurinol (reconciled by RN 5/21).

O: Vitals as charted. Left forearm volar and dorsal incisions closed, clean, no erythema. Hand: mild swelling, fingers warm, cap refill brisk, light touch intact, flexion limited about halfway. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Electrical injury with left forearm/hand compartment syndrome, s/p fasciotomy and closure. Healing well. OT and hand surgery follow-up per plan. Out of work until hand surgery clears him; note given.
2. Rhabdomyolysis/AKI: BMP and CK today. Expect normal.
3. Depression: some situational dip. Continue sertraline; we'll watch it. He knows he can message anytime.
4. Finish the oxycodone and stop; acetaminophen if needed after.

documents.title: Labs Normal
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Henry, creatinine 0.9 and CK 240, both normal. Your kidneys and muscles have recovered from the injury. Nothing else to do there. Good luck with OT next week.

documents.title: Hand Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: hand surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL HAND SURGERY CLINIC
Visit 06/11/2025

Mr. Silva returns four weeks after left forearm and hand fasciotomy with delayed closure following a high-voltage injury. Incisions fully healed. Edema minimal. Composite fist about 2 cm short of the palm, improving weekly with occupational therapy. Sensation intact in all digits. Grip weaker on the left.

Plan: continue OT twice weekly, scar massage. Remain off work. Return in 8 weeks.

Current meds: sertraline. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Work Form
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurer for his employer faxed a medical status form. PCP completed the general medical section (kidney recovered, no restrictions from our side) and noted work restrictions defer to hand surgery. Faxed back, copy scanned. Pt aware.

documents.title: Hand Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: hand surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL HAND SURGERY CLINIC
Visit 08/06/2025

Three months after left forearm and hand fasciotomy. Near-full range of motion of wrist and fingers, full fist. Grip close to the right side. Scars mature, no contracture. Neurovascularly intact.

Cleared to return to modified duty now, no heavy overhead lifting with the left arm for one more month, then full duty. Home exercise program; OT discharged. Discharged from hand clinic, return as needed.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza and 2025-26 COVID given, left and right deltoid. Tolerated. Back at work full duty since September, says the arm is basically normal. Waited 15 minutes.

documents.title: Call from Brother
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's older brother called. Henry was burned in a house fire early Wednesday and is in the burn ICU at a regional burn center. Brother says he has had a hard weekend but the team is managing. Asked us to know and to fax his med list and history. No release on file for the brother, so took his message only, confirmed nothing back. Called the burn unit and faxed med list/problem list to the unit clerk at their request. Flagged to PCP.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with Henry, home since yesterday, staying with his brother for now. Tired, sore, wearing garments. Pain pills about three a day. Eating well. Has dressing supplies, OT starts next week. Booked with PCP 1/6. Burn center summary not yet received, requested.

documents.title: Burn ICU Critical Care Note, Hospital Day 4
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL BURN CENTER, CRITICAL CARE PROGRESS NOTE
Date of service: 11/15/2025, hospital day 4

30 y/o M, construction worker, hx depression and hyperuricemia, prior kidney injury attributed to allopurinol (2024) and left forearm compartment syndrome after electrical injury (05/2025, fasciotomy). Admitted 11/12 with 40% TBSA burns from a house fire three days ago. Initial management: wound care and escharotomy, resuscitation with IV fluids, morphine for pain, prophylactic antibiotics. Enteral feeds since admission.

Events: Since early morning febrile, tachycardic and hypotensive. Complains of abdominal discomfort. Vomited twice; NG output 600 mL over the past 6 hours.

Home meds on file: sertraline 50 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.9 C, HR 120, BP 90/60.
Exam: Lethargic but arousable. Abdomen distended, tender to palpation, hypoactive bowel sounds. Dressings in place.

Labs: WBC 16.0, Hgb 10.2, Plt 250. Na 135, K 4.5, Cl 100, HCO3 22, BUN 28, Cr 1.4, glucose 110. Lactate 4.2.

Assessment: Septic shock on hospital day 4 of a 40% TBSA burn, source not yet identified. Feeding intolerance.
Plan: Blood and wound cultures, then broaden to vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Fluid bolus, norepinephrine to MAP 65 or more. Hold enteral feeds, NG to low intermittent suction. Serial lactate and abdominal exams. Continue sertraline when tolerating enteral route.

documents.title: Burn Center Discharge Summary
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL BURN CENTER, discharge summary
Admitted 11/12/2025. Discharged 12/23/2025 to home.

Diagnoses: 40% TBSA burns, house fire. Septic shock, hospital day 4, resolved; cultures negative.

Course: Escharotomy and wound care on arrival with fluid resuscitation. On day 4 developed fever, tachycardia, hypotension with lactate 4.2 and feeding intolerance. Treated with fluids, norepinephrine for about 48 hours, and vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam for 7 days. Blood and wound cultures grew no pathogen. Feeds were held with gastric decompression and restarted on day 7, tolerated, advanced to a regular diet. Excision and split-thickness skin grafting 11/19 and 12/02; grafts took well. Creatinine peaked at 1.4 and returned to normal. Physical and occupational therapy daily; walking independently at discharge.

Discharge labs 12/22: WBC 8.4, Hgb 10.9, creatinine 0.9.

Discharge medications: acetaminophen-oxycodone 325/5 mg every 6 hours as needed, short supply. Home meds continued: sertraline 50 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: burn clinic in 4-5 weeks; outpatient OT; pressure garments fitted before discharge, worn 23 hours a day; daily moisturizer and scar massage to grafted areas. PCP within 2 weeks. Off work until cleared by burn clinic.
